status: First pass, 18 October 2026. Game-balance numbers of the enemy air command (simcore/air_war/; docs/air_war/). Not system data.
source: game value: tuned by sam3d against the shapes in docs/research/ENEMY_AIR_RESEARCH_2026-10.md (staleness of mobile targets: wiki_model5; EMCON against ARMs: wiki_black_buck, vr_1985_plss; inflated claims: afmag_2000_kosovo, design reference only)
notes: Every key here is read by simcore/air_war (TuningTable::Defaults lists them with their defaults; an unknown key fails the load). Chances are per aircraft per pass unless said otherwise.

utility.notes: The planner's utility: value_weight x worth x chance it is there and works x chance of delivery x effect, minus loss_cost x expected losses x loss aversion (which grows as the faction's daily loss tolerance shrinks), plus quirk_scale x habits, minus the memory of losses that way, plus exploration x creativity / sqrt(1 + uses), plus noise that shrinks with planning skill. Packages below min_value are not flown. A cruise missile salvo has no crew to lose: missile_cost per missile spent, times the square root of how many times scarcer the stock has become than at the start (game value, the nation on the map N4, 23 Oct 2026). sortie_cost: per aircraft in a strike, DEAD or close-support package; above zero the planner weighs a pair, the template's group and a doubled one against each other (docs/air_war/13_PACKAGES.md): 0.1 sizes the groups to the target (a sweep of 0.05, 0.15 and 0.3 gave the Pact 7.9, 6.1 and 4.3 attackers a package, NATO 5.6, 4.9 and 4.1; docs/air_war/09_BALANCE.md section 10).

attrition.notes: low_vs_long_range_sam: a low flier is masked from a long-range SAM's radar (radius above 15 km) for most of a pass (Dugman 5's low approach traded SAMs for guns: wiki_model5). sead_suppression with two or more SEAD aircraft, scaled by the SEAD officer's skill and the package's coordination. night and poor_weather apply to optical defences. emcon_lethality: a SAM fighting silent (TV, the PU-12's designations) engages late. arm_kill_no_memory_off: an ARM without memory against a radar that switched off in time (wiki_black_buck); arm_kill_memory_off: one with a memory of where the radar was, which still misses most radars that radiate for seconds and move (Allied Force: some 743 HARMs, 3 of about 25 SA-6 batteries confirmed destroyed, rand_mr1365; calibrated in docs/air_war/09_BALANCE.md section 9). pass_scale: every defence's lethality is a relative one, times this for the chance per aircraft on a pass through the heart of its zone (calibrated against the period's losses in docs/air_war/09_BALANCE.md section 9: the 1973 belt, the Bekaa, Desert Storm's low against medium altitude). decoy_exposure: a radar that fired at decoys is suppressed at least this much by the SEAD behind them (the Bekaa, 1982). sead_suppression raised from 0.45 to 0.6 by the same calibration. An ARM's hit takes out one fire-control radar (an Osa battery has four). target_guns_troops and target_guns_site: light guns and shoulder-fired missiles around a target without its own air defence, per aircraft attacking it low or by helicopter (Dugman 5: most aircraft were hit by guns at the low approach height, wiki_model5); troops carry the most.

strike.notes: stale_miss_m: the aim point must be within this of the real target, or the bombs fall on empty ground (a battery that moved). decoy_area_m: a dummy this close to the aim point takes the bombs. collateral_m: bombs aimed this close to a town's edge risk civilian casualties.

delivery.notes: The weapons model (docs/air_war/10_WEAPONS.md). cep_*_m: the circular error of an unguided weapon by its attack, for a sight of middling quality (times 1.4 - 0.8 x the type's computing) and an average crew (times 1.25 - 0.5 x airmanship); the level figure is the Vietnam-era average miss (420-447 ft, afmag_2003_bombs), the guided ones the early Paveway (20 ft) and the TV seeker's ideal (wiki_lgb); the rest game values. night_visual_factor: a dive or pop-up by eye at night without a night attack system. cloudy_laser: the chance the laser spot holds under cloud. exposure_*: the share of the target's own guns and shoulder-fired missiles the attack meets (a laydown overflies them; a loft turns away some km short, saaf_toss; medium altitude is above them, rand_mr1365's 15,000 ft floor). release_*_m: how far short of the target the weapons go (a stand-off weapon at its own range). runway_strip_m: a crater anywhere this near the aim across the runway cuts it (about half a main runway's width), so a runway bomb's footprint is at least this. footprint_soft and footprint_light: a bomb's footprint against people, trucks and stores, and against light vehicles, radars and guns, times its footprint against armour and concrete (blast and fragments; game values). The attack profiles the routes fly: a pop-up pulls up popup_pull_m short of the target, climbs to popup_apex_m above the ground and releases in its dive at popup_release_m; a toss pulls up loft_pull_m out (4-5 nm, saaf_toss) and releases climbing at loft_release_m; a dive rolls in dive_roll_in_m short from its medium height and releases at dive_release_m (the MiG-27's level, dive and toss deliveries: mig27_book); a helicopter fires from the hover at hover_agl_m (game values). All game values, calibrated in docs/air_war/09_BALANCE.md section 9.

support.notes: The support aircraft (docs/air_war/11_SUPPORT.md). sorties_per_aircraft_day: what one support aircraft flies a day. An orbit kept round the clock takes awacs_sorties_per_orbit_day sorties of an AWACS (8-hour stations) and elint_sorties_per_orbit_day of an ELINT aircraft. receivers_per_tanker_sortie: Desert Storm's average was about 4.2 (215 KC-135 and 35 KC-10 sorties a day refuelled 1,061 aircraft, gwaps_vol3 Table 16). awacs_fighter_cut: the share of the defender's fighter chance an AWACS on station takes away (warning and vectoring for the escorts; game value). elint_reach_without and elint_sigma_without: the ELINT picture without an ELINT aircraft up, its reach and its error against one (game values). low_radius_share: the combat radius flown low against the type's published (lo-lo-lo against hi-lo-hi); refuelled_radius: with a tanker on the way (game values).

logistics.notes: Our supply lines (docs/air_war/14_LOGISTICS.md). consumption_per_day: a formation in the field uses a third of its stocks a day (three days of supply); once they are out it loses unsupplied_decay_per_day of its strength a day down to unsupplied_floor, and below repair_needs_supply mends nothing. bridge_open: a bridge carries traffic again from this function. snap_m: a depot or the troops this far off the country map's roads or railways reach them on local roads. search_m: an armed reconnaissance searches this far each way of its point along the line; find_*: the chance its pilots see a column on the move there, by day, at dawn or dusk, at night, at night with a night attack system, and times find_poor_weather under low cloud. All game values.

intel.notes: column_sigma_share: a supply column's believed position spreads at this share of its speed (it may have driven on or stopped). A mobile unit's believed position spreads at mobile_sigma_growth_mps and the belief that it is there halves every mobile_confidence_half_life_h. fixed_function_recovery: how fast the enemy assumes a struck fixed target is repaired (share per 48 h). ghost_fix_chance: an ELINT fix lands between the battery and a dummy whose decoy emitter radiates on its parameters (vr_1985_plss: active dummies). claim_destroy_when_off: pilots report a radar that went silent under ARM attack as destroyed.

adapt.notes: learning_rate is scaled by each officer's rigidity and method. An officer whose reputation falls below relieve_below is relieved; an ambitious one above promote_above is promoted away. reopen_margin: a campaign whose phase ended on the believed air defences goes back to it when they are believed this much above the line again (the rollback resumes when the sites come back).

politics.notes: Pressure from above grows on days without results; support falls with losses beyond the faction's tolerance; prisoners add pressure; civilian casualties widen the no-strike zone around towns (Rolling Thunder's restricted zones: nmusaf_sanctuaries).

repair.notes: Damage is repaired in the field at 1/repair_h of the whole an hour. A wrecked object is out until its replacement comes, repair_h after it was wrecked (a span, a battery from the reserve, new vehicles), and comes back at restored_function; the field repair completes it.

weather.notes: Each day's weather is drawn at the start: clear, cloudy or poor.

pacing.notes: Which of the enemy's raids the player flies: those that come within sector_m of the battery (or at it), no closer than min_gap_h apart, at most max_per_day. The rest are resolved abstractly. The pacing chooses; it never adds raids (l4d_director_2007, used only for this).

scenario.notes: A raid as the player's scenario: the flights inside clip_m of the battery, prep_s before the first aircraft appears; the mission bridge's weapon effects (roadmap E6 will replace the ARM with an EM missile).

own_intel.notes: What the player's side learns: a prisoner talks with pow_chance; the warning net gives warning_s before the first aircraft, leak_warning_s when the enemy's planner has loose lips.
